data.description:
## What was observed

A full `make verify` on 2026-09-04 in worktree `bug-9c93-ad8d-user-data-mounts` (a
`user_data.sh` mount-assertion change, zero overlap with the LLM gate path) reported:

```
31 failed, 19489 passed, 75 skipped, 14 warnings in 4131.23s (1:08:51)
```

28 of the 31 were `rebar.llm.errors.GateCongestedError: gate admission refused: all 4
concurrent slots busy`. The other 3 (`tests/unit/test_plan_review_cli_retry.py`,
`assert 11 == 2` on an LLM call count) were knock-on and passed in isolation.

**Re-running the 9 affected files ALONE still produced 14 failures.** That is the finding:
"run it alone" does not isolate this, so the usual triage step gives a FALSE "this is real
and it is mine" verdict.

## The mechanism

`rebar.llm.gate_admission._slot_dir()` returns `store_root() / "locks"`, and
`rebar._snapshot.repo_snapshot.store_root()` resolves to `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` **or else
`tempfile.gettempdir()`**. On a developer box with `REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` unset that is a single
directory shared by **every worktree, every session and every process on the machine**. The
four `gate-slot-N` files in it are therefore a HOST-GLOBAL semaphore, not a per-suite or
per-worktree one.

Two consequences:

1. The slots can be exhausted by processes that are **running no tests at all**.
2. Admission **fails closed WITHOUT waiting** — `_acquire_slot` returns `None` and the caller
   raises immediately (`gate_admission.py:305`, ":class:`GateCongestedError` without waiting
   when every slot is taken"). So a test needing a slot dies instantly rather than queueing
   behind the holder. Serialising the test run does not help; only freeing a slot does.

## Proof: who actually held the slots

Taken live with `lsof` on the four slot files while my own pytest count was **zero**:

| slot | PID | holder cwd | process |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gate-slot-0` | 50765 | `/Users/joeoakhart/janitor-e54e-shims` | `rebar verify-completion` |
| `gate-slot-1` | 6229 | `/Users/joeoakhart/janitor-f773-cli` | `rebar review-plan` |
| `gate-slot-2` | 20256 | `/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` | global `rebar-dev` release build |
| `gate-slot-3` | 89566 | `/Users/joeoakhart/janitor-038d-config` | `rebar` gate op |

All four were **other sessions' real 15-20 minute LLM gate operations**, in four different
worktrees. None was a test. None was mine. That is why the failures survived isolation, and
it is the part that a "concurrent xdist workers exhaust the suite's own slots" framing does
not predict: the exhausting processes need not be running the suite, or any suite.

## Scope: 31 tests across 9 files

This is not one test. Observed failing under contention:

- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_retry.py` (16)
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse.py` (6 under isolation; 1 in the full run)
- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_cli_retry.py` (3, knock-on `assert 11 == 2`)
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_producer_seam_8d8e.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/test_pinned_ticket_view.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/test_gate_peak_rss_9ea3.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py` (2)
- `tests/unit/test_eval_solver.py` (1)
- `tests/unit/workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar.py` (1)

This directly answers AC4 of `torrential-unwhite-snail` (`9c2e-b44c-119e-4105`), which asked
for "a check that no other test in the suite has the same host-wide coupling, or a ticket
filed for any that do". They do; this is that ticket.

## CI consequence

These tests are red whenever four real gate ops are in flight anywhere on the same machine —
**including in CI if a runner is ever shared, or if a self-hosted runner also hosts gate
work**. The failure names gate congestion, so it reads as an infrastructure problem rather
than a test defect, which is exactly the shape that gets `recheck`ed instead of fixed. Per
AGENTS.md that makes it a bug to root-cause, not a retry candidate: it is reproducible by
construction (occupy all four slots, run the tests), not random.

## Proposed fix direction

Give the test suite its **own** slot directory rather than the host's, by pointing
`REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR` at a per-session temp dir in the test fixture. That is a one-line
environment change at the fixture level and needs no change to `gate_admission`'s logic, so
it keeps the production semantics (a genuinely shared host semaphore) exactly as they are
while removing the cross-session coupling from the tests.

**Not implemented here deliberately.** It touches the gate-admission path that several agent
sessions are exercising concurrently right now, and the change that surfaced it was about
`user_data.sh` mounts. Keeping them separate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - The coupling is reproduced deterministically: occupy all 4 host slots from a
      process that runs no tests, then run the 9 files above and observe the same failures.
      This must be a real reproduction, not an assumption from the field evidence.
- [ ] AC2 - The listed tests pass with all four HOST slots held by an unrelated process.
- [ ] AC3 - What each test actually asserts is still asserted. The fix must not be skipping,
      deleting, or `xfail`ing them, and must not weaken gate admission itself.
- [ ] AC4 - Production semantics are unchanged: a real gate op on a real host still contends
      for a shared, host-wide semaphore. The isolation applies to the TEST suite only.
- [ ] AC5 - Some guard stops a future test re-acquiring the host-global slot silently, so the
      class does not simply grow back.
data.title: Gate admission's 4 slots are HOST-GLOBAL (store_root()/locks under tempfile.gettempdir()), so ~31 unit tests across 9 files go red whenever any process on the box holds a real gate op
